questions.stem_text: Why is it important to separate the concept of punishment from its justification?

options.A: Because the concept of punishment has evolved over time.
options.B: Because punishment can be justified in multiple ways.
options.C: Because any definition of punishment should be value-neutral.
options.D: Because the practice of punishment is separate from its justification.
options.E: Because the justification of punishment varies across cultures.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: C - Because any definition of punishment should be value-neutral.

questions.stem_text:
In which instance would a state, under the enabling clause of the Fourteenth Amendment, be
most able to regulate?

options.A: A federal official from discriminating against a person based on race.
options.B: A federal official from discriminating against a person based on gender.
options.C: A federal official from discriminating against a person based on nationality.
options.D: A private company from discriminating against a person based on nationality.
options.E: A private individual from discriminating against a person based on race.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - A federal official from discriminating against a person based on race.

questions.stem_text:
Catharine MacKinnon argues that since men dominate women, the question is ultimately one
of power. Which proposition below is the most inconsistent with this argument?

options.A: The power dynamic is determined by individual strength and not gender.
options.B: The idea of 'woman' needs to be redefined.
options.C: Women inherently possess more power than men.
options.E: Men and women share equal power in society.

questions.answer_explanation: Correct option: A - The power dynamic is determined by individual strength and not gender.
